segments.text: I'm the founder of Quiet Protector and a lot of people ask me what the difference is between
Terrashell and all those cheap space blankets out there.
So here's the short version.
Terrashell isn't a flimsy foil blanket.
There is really no comparison.
Most emergency space blankets are kind of exactly what you think.
Thin, crinkly Mylar sheets that rip the second you shift around.
Bright reflective orange so you look like a traffic cone and completely open on the
side.
So freezing drafts blow right through.
Terrashell is something entirely different.
We engineered it around the full hypothermia wrap protocol used in wilderness medicine and
search and rescue.
It is a full body Vivian closure with an aluminized radiative mirror lining that reflects 90%
of your body heat back to your core, sealed inside a windproof and waterproof tactical
shell.
Plus, Terrashell is finished in a matte army green instead of bright orange foil.
So you keep your privacy and peace of mind during a crisis.
Every scene is reinforced to keep out wet snow and freezing air.
There are no batteries to die, no fuel tanks to fill and nothing mechanical that can break
down on you.
It relies purely on thermodynamics to keep you warm.
You can use it in your living room when the power grid fails and the house drops
to 40 degrees.
You can keep it in your glove box for highway breakdowns in a blizzard.
It weighs just four ounces, packs down smaller than a soda can and creates an instant warm
microclimate around you in seconds, reflecting 90% of your heat while regular cotton blankets
actually pull warmth away from your body.
